messages:
Miguel: ran an nsys capture against staging-serving-3 (pinned drivers enabled) to investigate the weird latency spike in the KV-prefetch path. Initial observation: large serialization on peercopy + lots of tiny H2D bursts. trace: https://internal-artifacts/nsys/1967894321.nsys :eyes:

perf-bot: nsys summary: total GPU H2D bandwidth drop ~30% during spike window; top kernels by time: memcpyAsync (host->device), cuMemcpyPeerAsync, kernel-launch stalls due to stream serialization. Detected fallback to pageable memcpy for ~12% of transfers.

Ciara: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet for the hotspot window? curious if streams are actually concurrent or queued on the host.

Miguel: timeline excerpt (0.120s window):
```
0.000s - host memcpyAsync (4KB) queued on stream 3 -> device H2D (nvLink)
0.0005s - host memcpyAsync (2KB) queued on stream 4 -> device H2D
0.0012s - cuMemcpyPeerAsync (batched) invoked from same host thread -> appears serialized
0.0030s - kernel A (kv_prefetch) waits on stream 3
0.0035s - host memcpy falls back to pageable path: memcpy (glibc) -> long CPU copy ~0.6ms
0.0041s - subsequent memcpyAsync calls pile up, host thread becomes a bottleneck
```

Ashley: this looks like the classic pageable fallback causing host-side serialization. Two contributing factors I see: 1) allocator for prefetch buffers sometimes returns non-pinned pages (small allocations), and 2) the batching heuristic sends many tiny memcopies instead of coalescing them. :thinking_face:

Riya: repro notes: I ran a controlled job with KV prefetch generating 3000 small keys (typical size 512B-4KB). With default allocator p99 latency -> 420ms. When I enabled pinned allocations for the prefetch slab (cudaHostAlloc) p99 -> ~110-130ms and H2D bandwidth normalized. So pinned memory avoids the synchronous CPU copy path.

Jon: a couple of suggestions:
- runtime: add a cheap heuristic to prefer pinned allocations for the prefetch slab if avg_transfer_size < 8KB OR transfer_count_in_window > 256
- batcher: coalesce adjacent prefetch keys into a single larger transfer when possible (merge contiguous KV pages)
- kernel selection: prefer cuMemcpyAsync/cuMemcpyPeerAsync for > 4KB, but force pinned memcpy path for <= 4KB to avoid fallback.

Jon: pseudocode for batcher tweak:
```
if (sum_transfer_bytes_in_window < 64KB && distinct_transfers > 64) {
  coalesce_into_single_buffer(); // reduce number of host->device calls
}
```

Ciara: nice. Any downside to enabling pinned by default for prefetch? memory pressure / fragmentation?

Riya: tradeoffs: pinned pages can reduce system DRAM locality and cause GPU DMA pressure; we saw ~6% extra host memory usage in the repro. But we can make it opt-in per deployment (Dedicated/Private) or behind our runtime flag with telemetry. Also implement a slab with eviction for pinned pages.

Miguel: numbers from quick run (same workload):
- baseline (malloc): p50 18ms, p95 210ms, p99 420ms
- pinned slab: p50 20ms, p95 85ms, p99 120ms
Bandwidth graphs show H2D drop removed and no long CPU memcpy spikes.

Ashley: action items:
1) runtime: add pinned slab behind env var REDWOOD_PREFETCH_PINNED=true + stats (Riya)
2) batcher: implement coalescing heuristic and unit test (Jon)
3) perf: run full nsys capture with nvlink counters enabled and longer window (Miguel)
4) ops: flag Dedicated customers for beta pinned option (Product)

Miguel: I'll upload the full nsys file and a perfetto timeline to the run folder and open a minimal repro harness in /infra/kv-prefetch-repros. Will post links when done. :thumbsup:

Ashley: thanks — please include a short perf checklist in the PR (what to measure p50/p95/p99 and bandwidth counters). I'll review the PR once Miguel posts it. :party_parrot:
